stem: A 62-year-old man has 45 minutes of tearing interscapular chest pain and is diaphoretic. The left radial pulse is weak and the left femoral is absent. CT aortogram shows a Stanford type A dissection and cardiothoracic surgery is 20 minutes away.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse 118 /min, blood pressure 218/122 mmHg right arm and 178/106 mmHg left arm

lead_in: What is the most appropriate immediate pharmacological management?

options.text: Verapamil 5 mg intravenously targeting a heart rate under 60
options.rationale: Verapamil is used only when beta blockers are contraindicated; esmolol or labetalol are first line for their titratable pharmacology and preferred agents in AU practice. (Source: eTG: Aortic dissection)

options.text: Glyceryl trinitrate infusion to systolic 100 to 120 mmHg alone
options.rationale: Vasodilator before rate control causes reflex tachycardia and increases aortic wall shear stress, propagating the dissection; beta blockade must precede vasodilator therapy in dissection. (Source: AHA/ACC aortic dissection guideline 2022)

options.text: Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg for a suspected coronary thrombus
options.rationale: This is aortic dissection and troponin is negative; thrombolysis in aortic dissection can extend the dissection and cause fatal haemorrhage and is absolutely contraindicated. (Source: AHA/ACC aortic dissection guideline 2022)

options.text: Fentanyl alone, holding antihypertensives until theatre
options.rationale: Untreated hypertension propagates the dissection and increases the risk of rupture and death during the 20 minute wait for theatre; blood pressure and heart rate control are urgent alongside analgesia. (Source: AHA/ACC aortic dissection guideline 2022)

options.text: Esmolol to heart rate under 60, then glyceryl trinitrate
options.rationale: Aortic dissection requires heart rate reduction before vasodilation to reduce dP/dt and shear stress; unopposed vasodilator causes reflex tachycardia and worsens propagation. Target heart rate under 60 and systolic 100-120 mmHg. Esmolol first, then GTN or sodium nitroprusside added. (Source: eTG: Aortic dissection; AHA/ACC aortic dissection guideline 2022)

explanation.summary: Acute aortic dissection is managed by simultaneously controlling heart rate then blood pressure to reduce dP/dt and aortic wall shear stress. First line is intravenous beta blocker (esmolol infusion, or labetalol) titrated to heart rate under 60 before adding an intravenous vasodilator (GTN or sodium nitroprusside) to bring systolic blood pressure to 100-120 mmHg. Type A dissections (ascending aorta involved) are surgical emergencies with mortality of 1-2% per hour untreated; type B dissections are usually managed medically with intervention for complications (malperfusion, rupture, refractory pain or hypertension). Thrombolysis is absolutely contraindicated.
key_points: Aortic dissection dP/dt reduction: rate first then vasodilator
Target: heart rate under 60, systolic 100-120 mmHg
Type A: immediate surgery. Type B: medical unless complications
Thrombolysis is absolutely contraindicated in aortic dissection
explanation.pearls: Blood pressure differential between arms of more than 20 mmHg, absent limb pulse, or new aortic regurgitation with tearing pain is dissection until proven otherwise, and time to imaging saves lives.
